data.body:
Phase 1 disposition — environment-or-config; no code repair is proven.

Problem: an earlier unchanged-tree suite completed 16,691 tests but two autouse repo-isolation teardown probes exceeded the fixed five-second git rev-parse HEAD watchdog. The instrumented investigation ran from current origin/main 8cbf31007a35; the probe code was unchanged from the reported base and remains unchanged through 7383663d4a39.

Runtime evidence and latency: 1,000 sequential real probes measured p50 9.6 ms, p90 13.1 ms, p99 67 ms, max 507 ms. Under 18 processes x 100 probes, p99 was 2.08 s and max 3.30 s. In the seven-arm 5,400-call-per-arm experiment, /usr/bin/true maxed at 149 ms, git --version at 714 ms, independent repos at 939 ms, shared worktree at 1.18 s, linked worktrees at 636 ms, shared ref churn at 1.75 s, and linked ref churn at 1.05 s. Popen itself stayed below 183 ms; the long tail accumulated after exec while the child ran or waited. Shared common-dir/ref activity contributes to the tail but did not independently reproduce the five-second event.

The observational full-suite run raised only the diagnostic ceiling to 30 seconds and logged real probes over one second or any error. It completed 16,684 passed, 64 skipped, 298 deselected in 6,266.18 s; the three reported failures were expected effects of temporary instrumentation, not product regressions. Sixteen real successful probes crossed one second (1.004–1.686 s); none crossed two or five seconds. Every one resolved /opt/homebrew/bin/git, carried the same PATH digest, had all recorded Git control variables unset, returned the expected 8cbf31007a35 SHA, and appeared across unrelated setup/teardown nodes. The exact two previously failing nodes pass serially. This rejects PATH/Git-environment contamination and test-local state as explanations.

The discriminating host evidence is severe shared-host oversubscription. The machine has 18 logical CPUs. From sampler start through the last suite probe, one-minute load was p50 76.4, p90 110.8, p99 138.2, max 170; process count was p50 730 and max 771; total sampled CPU was p50 1,614%, and Python/pytest CPU alone p50 1,288%. One real guard probe failed immediately with OSError: no resources to fork. Slow successful probes correlate with the same saturated interval. Combined with the timeout occurring only after Popen, this identifies scheduler/filesystem starvation on the shared overloaded host as the mechanism.

Alternatives: ordinary quiet-host latency is rejected by the sequential distribution; pure process-creation delay is rejected by Popen timing; shared-repository contention contributes but is insufficient alone in controlled arms; inherited PATH/Git variables and monkeypatched Git are rejected by the recorded runtime identity and environment.

Legitimacy: environment-or-config, not a proven product defect. callous-amused-hart is the authoritative contract: the fixed five-second watchdog must bound a blocked local child and timeout must fail explicitly. The later run did not observe a successful probe above five seconds, so it cannot support changing that contract. Raising the watchdog would trade away the deliberate hang bound and mask host exhaustion without a proven safe calibration.

Disposition: no repo-isolation repair. All DEBUG-rebar-debug instrumentation was removed and the worktree restored clean. A second 104-minute suite was deliberately not launched because it would exacerbate the saturation being investigated and one additional green run cannot reject a rare tail. The operational mitigation is to avoid overlapping full suites or cap aggregate pytest/agent concurrency on this 18-core host. If the watchdog contract itself should change, that requires an explicit operator design decision and a stated post-change bound; the present evidence does not authorize it.
